master.title: Serbia: Afternoon Media Review 17.3.2022
master.content:
EU in Serbia 


Joksimovic: Serbia was not guided by shortcuts to EU membership 

Serbia has achieved significant results in joining the European Union, said Minister of European Integration Jadranka Joksimovic, adding that Cluster 3 - Competitiveness and Inclusive Growth is fully ready and could be opened during the French EU Presidency, which lasts until June 30. In an interview with Telegraf.rs, Joksimovic stated that in the context of current events in Ukraine, it is expected and common sense from the point of view of geopolitical, geoeconomic and geostrategic reasons that the EU starts intensified action towards strengthening peace, democracy and stronger dynamics of European integration processes in the region of the Western Balkans. She pointed out that Serbia achieved significant results in joining the EU and that everything we have achieved in that process is the result of our work. "The fact that we are making progress in such circumstances and that we are leading the process, shows that our country is a really serious and credible partner of the EU and Serbia in that regard shows undoubted capacity and political determination," Joksimovic said. She pointed out that the Government of Serbia was not guided by thoughts about "shortcuts for membership", but that it was focused exclusively from the beginning on results that bring benefits to all citizens of our country. 

Source: Tvmost.info, Telegraf.rs 


Brnabic: Our principled position on Ukraine is not fully welcomed by Russia either 

Prime Minister Ana Brnabic underlined today that Serbia's principled stance regarding the condemnation of the violation of Ukraine's territorial integrity, but without sanctions on Russia, is not something that is fully welcomed by the European Union or by other partners, including Russia. "That is the position of a country that has been under sanctions for many years, which is why ordinary citizens have suffered the most. They also suffered the most because of the aggression of NATO countries. So Serbia is in a very specific situation which, despite all the pressures, fully respects international law and its principles," Brnabic said in a joint address with Austrian Chancellor Karl Nehammer. Asked whether the relations between Serbia and Russia have changed due to the war in Ukraine, she stated that the relations between the two countries are traditionally very good, because we are connected by history, culture, tradition, religion, and nowadays some things such as energy industry. She pointed out that the war in Ukraine affects the economy of Serbia, because 75% of our economy consists of companies from the EU, and they must implement sanctions against Russia. So, for example, if you have a cement plant owned by an EU company, it cannot import or export anything to Russia, like any other EU company. All these companies, in their internal business, regardless of what they do in Serbia, they adhere to the sanctions imposed by their governments, i.e. the EU. That is a great challenge for our economy," Brnabic emphasised. 

Source: Nova.rs, Rs.n1info.com 


Joksimovic and Van den Ende on European integration 

The Minister for European Integration, Jadranka Joksimovic, talked today in Belgrade with the delegation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, led by the Director General of the Directorate for European Cooperation, Anita van den Ende, about Serbia's European integration. Reforms in the field of the rule of law and strengthening democracy in our country were especially discussed, as well as the current security situation in Europe and relations in the region. "We have started the procedure of preparing draft laws and bylaws which will implement the reform of the judiciary, envisaged by the amendments to the Constitution, in the legal system of Serbia," Joksimovic emphasised. She also pointed out that Serbia fully prepared Cluster 3 - Competitiveness and inclusive growth, and continued to work on other clusters, primarily on reaching the criteria for opening Cluster 5 - Resources, agriculture and cohesion, but also those in Cluster 2 - Internal market. Anita van den Ende stated that the Netherlands supports the reform processes in Serbia as an EU candidate country, advocating the principle that all criteria from the accession process must be reached by the end of negotiations, especially those related to the rule of law, strengthening democracy and media freedoms. She also stressed that EU member states expect greater harmonisation of Serbia as a candidate country for EU membership with the Union's Common Foreign and Security Policy. 

Source: Gradskeinfo.rs, Srpskaekonomija.rs 


Nikola Jovanovic meets the cabinet of Oliver Varhelyi in Brussels 

Director of the Centre for Local Self-Government (CLS) Nikola Jovanovic met with Sabolc Horvat, chief expert in the cabinet of European Commissioner for Enlargement and Neighbourhood Policy Oliver Varhelyi. Maja Kocijancic, political advisor in the cabinet, also participated in the meeting. "The impact of the war in Ukraine on Serbia and the Western Balkans was discussed, but above all on regional cooperation and the reform process in Serbia," it was stated. 

Source: Rs.n1info.com, Direktno.rs 

 

Micovic: We should get an interpretation from the EU regarding sanctions 

The Secretary General of the Association of Oil Companies of Serbia, Tomislav Micovic, says that lawyers have yet to interpret the new EU sanctions imposed on Russia and whether they refer to NIS. Micovic reminds that NIS is majority owned by Gazprom Neft, as well as that NIS is very important for the supply of the Serbian market. "That could be a potential problem, if the import of oil or derivatives for NIS was stopped," said Micovic. He mentioned that it should be borne in mind that NIS is, after all, a Serbian company with its headquarters in Serbia. "We need to study the regulation carefully and we still need lawyers to interpret it, as well as to get an interpretation from the EU who it refers to," Micovic said for Prva. 

Source: Rtv.rs, 021.rs 


Joint message of NGOs from Serbia and Kosovo: Change the paradigm of EU enlargement 

Russia's invasion of Ukraine raises deep concerns in the Western Balkans, which is particularly vulnerable to global developments, 29 civil society organisations and individuals from Serbia and Kosovo said, urging the EU and member states to change the enlargement paradigm, but also to "rethink" the dialogue between Belgrade and Pristina. The joint statement said Russia's invasion of Ukraine had negatively affected the rules-based international order, and that the Western Balkans was particularly vulnerable to global developments that threatened international law, democracy and human rights. "We, the representatives of civil society organisations from Kosovo and Serbia, condemn Russia's aggression against Ukraine and call on our governments to join the position of the European Union," they said in a statement. They call on the EU and its member states to change the enlargement paradigm, "to ensure a practical and proactive approach to the European perspective of the Western Balkans". 

Source: Rs.n1info.com, Euronews.rs 


Nehammer: Austria is a bridge between the EU and Serbia 

Austrian Chancellor Karl Nehammer said in Belgrade today that his country would continue to strive to be a bridge between the EU and Serbia and other Western Balkan countries. At a joint press conference after meeting with Serbian Prime Minister Ana Brnabic, Nehammer said that because of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, it was "important for Serbia and other countries in the region that the EU takes a clear stance" and gives a clear signal that those countries that they belong to the Union and Europe. "As the EU, we must do everything to speed up the accession process (of the Western Balkans). Austria sees itself as a bridge in that process, it is very important for us to speed up that process," Nehammer said. He stated that relations with Serbia are "of great importance" for Austria and added that Serbia is "a geostrategically and geopolitically important partner for Austria, and thus for the EU." "It is very important for Austria that we work together because we are equally affected by the phenomenon of organised crime and the phenomenon of illegal migration. It is also the interest of one EU member state to give a clear signal that we need to work together to find a solution to the problems," said the Austrian chancellor. He announced the deepening of bilateral cooperation and pointed out that the Serbian market is "very interesting" for Austria and the EU. 

Source: Danas.rs, Novimagazin.rs 



 Serbian Politics 

 

Petkovic: 2004 pogrom was aimed at obliterating all traces of Kosovo Serbs' existence 

The head of the Serbian government Office for Kosovo and Metohija Petar Petkovic on Thursday said March 17, 2004 was one of the most difficult days in Serbia's recent history as, on that day, ethnic Albanians in Kosovo had been aiming to obliterate all traces of the existence of Serbs in the province. "In an outburst of hatred, attacks and a wave of violence by ethnic Albanian extremists, 19 people were killed, 4,012 Serbs were expelled from their ancestral homes, 935 Serb homes were destroyed and 35 churches, monasteries and monastery dwellings, including some mediaeval ones, were burned down and razed," Petkovic told the RTS, adding that the pogrom had taken place "right in front of the eyes of the international community." He said the Church of Our Lady of Ljevis - included in a UNESCO list of world cultural heritage - had been burned down as well. "Those who had the duty to protect the Serb population in Kosovo and Metohija looked on as that population fled to escape hordes of Albanian extremists. March 17 is a stain on the face of the international community," Petkovic said, adding that no one had been called to account for the plight of Serbs and the torching of Serbian Orthodox churches and monasteries. He said Serbia insisted on justice being served. "Until the murderers and those who gave the orders are found, the government will not give up on the quest for truth and justice. The ideology of hatred of 2004 was a very coordinated action aimed at expelling the Serb population," Petkovic said. The March 17-18, 2004 pogrom was, in fact, the second large pogrom committed by the ethnic Albanians against the Kosovo Serbs, the first one being the mass expulsion that followed the 1999 NATO bombing of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. 

Source: Rts.rs, 24sedam.rs 

 

Ponos agrees to appear on TV Pink 

Opposition presidential candidate Zdravko Ponos has decided to appear on the TV Pink even though other opposition leaders are refusing to appear on that station considered close to the authorities. TV Pink owner Zeljko Mitrovic offered a short daily slot to political parties as part of the election campaign. I will present my presidential candidacy on TV Pink on Thursday, March 24 at 5:30 pm, Ponos wrote on his Twitter account. Earlier, Ponos declined an invitation to appear on the station, citing prior engagements. 

Source: Danas.rs, Nova.rs 

 

CINS sets up data base for political financing 

The Serbian Centre for Investigative Journalism (CINS) has set up a data base on the financing of political parties and groups allowing users to track the money. The data base titled Party Coffer (Stranacka kasa) includes data on 25 parties and groups that spent 8 billion Dinars in budget funds between 2015 and 2021. It shows that 3.6 billion of that amount was spent on advertising alone. The data base includes information on budget funds, private money, company funds, property rentals and expenses for advertising, rentals and training. These are the expenses of some of the most influential parties and groups which have been reviewed by the Anti-Corruption Agency, CINS said. It said that the data was taken from financial reports published on party web sites and the Anti-Corruption Agency registry. CINS said that data base would be kept updated. 

Source: Cins.rs 

 

TV N1 invites Vucic and Ponos to presidential debate 

N1 TV invited President of Serbia Aleksandar Vucic and opposition presidential candidate Zdravko Ponos to an election campaign duel. Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) candidate for Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic often says in his public appearance that no different opinions are heard on N1 TV, that is the views of the authorities. He has been repeating that frequently in the election campaign. N1 wants to inform the public that it has been continuously inviting representatives of the authorities to appear on our shows ever since we went on the air in 2014. Aleksandar Vucic has received dozens of invitations and we have repeated them in this election campaign, both to him personally and to members of the SNS. No one from Aleksandar Vucic s team has replied to the invitation to appear on the 360 Degrees show on March 17 which will offer presidential candidates an opportunity to present their programmes, N1 said. That is why we are inviting him once again to benefit from this opportunity and take part in a live show on N1 TV in a duel with the most prominent opposition candidate Zdravko Ponos. We feel that voters in Serbia, before they decide who to vote for, have the right to see the most prominent candidates confront each other with their views. That is the heritage of contemporary states which contributes to democracy. We reserved the 9 pm slot on March 29 for the presidential duel, it added. 

Source: Rs.n1info.com 

 

Tadic: State could not have prevented 2004 pogrom of Kosovo Serbs 

Boris Tadic, the leader of the Social Democratic Party and former president of Serbia, stated on March 17 that Serbian state institutions could not have prevented the pogrom of Serbs in Kosovo which took place in March 2004, because any military or police operation in the province would have entailed conflict with KFOR i.e. NATO. Speaking for Prva TV on the 18th anniversary of the brutal attacks against Kosovo Serbs, Tadic said that, at the time, Serbia did not have the capacity for a military reaction but that the country did use military diplomacy, which resulted in NATO s intervention on the second day of the pogrom. The former president further stated that violence against Serbs has become somewhat legalised since 1999 and the arrival of KFOR in Kosovo, citing both UNMIK s and KFOR s tacit approval. 

Source: Nedeljnik.rs, Novimagazin.rs 

 

Teachers Union protests in front of Education Ministry 

The USPRS teachers union staged a protest at noon on Thursday in front of the Serbian Education Ministry in Belgrade. The teachers are demanding smaller classes, the pay grades they have been calling for since 2015 and quality education. Education in Serbia has been degraded, Education Minister Branko Ruzic is not doing his job and no one is thinking about the future of education in Serbia, one of the teachers said and recalled that they have been protesting with the same demands for years. According to the teachers, the pandemic showed the bad situation in the education system. The protest was accompanied by a strike in some schools in the rest of the country where classes have been shortened. 

Source: Rs.n1info.com 

                                                          


 International relations/foreign policy 

 

 

Brnabic: Austria significant partner, Serbia pillar of stability 

Austria is a significant political and economic partner of Serbia, PM Ana Brnabic said after a meeting with Austrian Chancellor Karl Nehammer on Thursday, noting that she had told Nehammer Serbia was a pillar of peace and stability in the Western Balkans. At a joint press conference, Brnabic said the meeting reaffirmed the partnership and friendship between Serbia and Austria, as well as their strong political and economic ties, Austria being one of Serbia's closest partners. She thanked Austria for supporting Serbia's European integration, and noted that former Chancellor Sebastian Kurz had done much for Serbia and the Western Balkans in that regard. "We have always had a partner to rely on in Austria," Brnabic noted. Economically, Austria is the second-largest foreign investor in Serbia behind Germany, Brnabic said. She said Austrian companies had invested 2.585 bln euros in Serbia to date and were employing over 22,000 people in the country in total. She said bilateral trade with Austria had been worth 1.36 bln euros in 2021, or 28 pct more relative to 2020. She said the bilateral trade volume had grown by 1.7 times between 2010 and 2020 while Serbian exports to Austria had increased by 1.9 times and imports from Austria by 1.8 times. "That is an encouraging trend that is good for all citizens," Brnabic said. She said they had also discussed the war in the east of Europe. "We had an open conversation. I know many in the EU are worried about instability spilling over to the Western Balkans. I noted clearly that Serbia will continue to play the role of a country that is a pillar of stability in the Western Balkans, that we will continue to be exporters of peace and stability and that we will not allow instability or the crisis to spill over to this part of Europe," Brnabic also said. 

Source: Tanjug.rs, Novosti.rs 

 

Zakharova: Biden ordered the bombing of Belgrade 

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova published a video of the 1998 meetings of the US Senate Foreign Relations Committee. According to Zakharova, the video was made a year before the bombing of Belgrade. The video shows the current president of the USA, Joe Biden, saying that it was he who proposed the bombing of the capital of the then FR Yugoslavia. "I suggested bombing of Belgrade. I suggested that American pilots go there and destroy all bridges on the Drina," Biden said. Zakharova states that Biden talks about it even before the bombing, explaining that Belgrade was bombed. "Yugoslavia did not pose a direct or indirect threat to the United States or its citizens. They just needed it," Zakharova concluded. 

Source: B92.net, Nsuzivo.rs 

 

Pristina can hardly join NATO now, especially not the EU 

Stefan Surlic from the Faculty of Political Sciences (FPN), stated that he does not believe that at this moment, Pristina could fulfil its demands for membership in NATO, and especially in the EU. "Countries that do not recognise the independence of Kosovo, which are members of the EU and NATO, do so for the clear reason that no final agreement has been reached between Belgrade and Pristina, and as long as there is no such agreement, I think there will be no political courage or strength for any of these political leaders to change the decision not to recognise Kosovo's independence due to external pressure," Surlic said. He believes that the pressure to reach an agreement will continue, because there is a fear, above all of a homogenised Western bloc, that the frozen conflicts on European soil could be unfrozen in these extraordinary circumstances. "This is also a key fear in the context of Serbian-Albanian relations, so we have special attention and visits of Western envoys to the Western Balkans to offer some credible prospect of EU membership, i.e. its strategic partnership with EU member states, in order to prevent any security dilemma," said Surlic. Asked whether increased pressure on Serbia to impose sanctions on Russia can be expected, Surlic reminded that our position is that until we become a full member of the EU, we have no obligation to harmonise with Brussels' foreign and security policy, but that circumstances have changed. 

Source: B92.net 

 

Popovic with Botsan-Kharchenko: Serbia will not impose sanctions on Russia 

At the meeting with the Russian ambassador in Belgrade, Alexander Botsan-Kharchenko, the Minister without portfolio in the Government of Serbia, Nenad Popovic, reiterated the position that Serbia will not impose sanctions on Russia, his cabinet announced. Popovic, the minister in charge of innovation and technological development, talked with Botsan-Kharchenko about ways to overcome the practical problems of the economy and citizens in the newly created regional and global circumstances. 

Source: Danas.rs, Rs.n1info.com 

 

Where are the Russians fleeing through the "Serbian door"? Which destinations are the most interesting for them? 

Russian carriers do not fly to Europe due to EU sanctions, which Brussels imposed due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and European carriers do not fly to Russia. By rejecting the sanctions, Serbia has become an air corridor, open to Russian citizens who are fleeing their homeland en masse through the "Serbian door". Russians who fly to Serbia often do not stay there, but travel further to Europe. According to the analysis of the travel agency Forwardkeys, in the first week of March, compared to the week before the Russian invasion of Ukraine, occupancy on flights between Russia and Serbia increased by 50 percent, and compared to the period before the pandemic, demand increased by 200 percent. "In our analysis, the speed with which Serbia became the starting point for travel between Russia and Europe stands out the most," said Olivier Ponti, the agency's vice president. Air Serbia currently flies to Russia 15 times a week, three times a week. Russians who land in Serbia often do not stay there, but travel further to Europe, according to the analysis of Forwardkeys, their final destinations are primarily Montenegro, Cyprus, France, Switzerland and Italy, less "popular" are Spain, Germany, Austria and Slovenia. 

Source: Rs.n1info.com 

 


Economy, investments and trade 

 


First container shipment on the Danube to the Port of Constanta 

DP World Novi Sad has successfully completed the testing of the first container shipment on the Danube between the ports of Novi Sad in Serbia and Constanta in Romania. The first ship, Vigilla, transported over 50 containers to the Port of Novi Sad last weekend, where the goods were quickly and successfully loaded onto trucks for the delivery to end customers, the company says in a press release. This is the first step toward the establishment of the new DP World Novi Sad service, which will secure a safer and simpler ecological transport of goods for the customers. DP World, a leading provider of smart logistics solutions in the world, became the owner of the Port of Novi Sad in May 2019 and obliged to invest EUR 35 million in a range of extensions and development, such as the new service of the transport on the Danube to the Port of Constanta. The company is also building a new container terminal at the port, which includes the construction of new silos for the storage of goods, the reconstruction of roads and the expansion of the vertical dock. 

Source: Rtv.rs, Tanjug.rs 

 

Crude sunflower seed oil exempted from export ban 

The Serbian government adopted today the amended Decree on limiting the prices of petroleum products, which allows companies specialising in trade in motor and other fuels at petrol stations to deliver fuel not only by filling the tanks of vehicles, but also by pouring the fuel into vessels for the transport of petroleum products in the maximum amount of 60 litres. This enables, first and foremost, farmers who use agricultural machines as means of work to continue to perform their work without hindrance. The current decision, as well as changes to this decision, have been made in order to prevent major disturbances and preserve the living standards of the population. The Serbian government also adopted the amended Decision on the temporary ban on the export of basic agricultural food products important to the population, which exempts crude oil from sunflower seed or saffron from the export ban, given that this product cannot be further used for processing into refined sunflower oil and is most commonly used in the paint and varnish industry. It was also decided to add refined sunflower oil to the list of products whose export is temporarily banned. 

Source: Espreso.rs, Danas.rs 

 


Energy and environment 

 

Import and prices of energy sources, export and inflation biggest challenges for the economy 

The delegation of the mission of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which is visiting Serbia, led by Jan Kees Martijn, has talked to representatives of the Chamber of Commerce of Serbia (CCIS) about macroeconomic and financial stability, investment environment and the challenges which lie ahead of the Serbian economy due to the Ukrainian crisis and the global market disturbances. As pointed out at the meeting, the problems that the EU economy is facing are also the ones that worry the Serbian economy the most, namely, the import and the growth of the prices of energy sources and other raw materials, exporting, supply chains and inflation, according to the website of the CCIS. Serbia shares the fate of the whole Europe and European companies and it is very important to precisely look into which industries are the most jeopardised, where the state can help overcome the crisis as easily as possible and what is cause for alarm, said Mihailo Vesovic, the director of the Sector for Strategic Analyses, Services and Internationalisation of the CCIS, following the conversation with the IMF representatives. At the meeting at the CCIS, there was talk about how the Serbian economy is handling the current crisis and which consequences and impacts on the so far accelerated economic development and GDP growth are expected. 

Source: Ekapija.com, Vesti-online.com 

 


Society and Chronicle 

 

Coronavirus update: 14 deaths, 2,362 new cases 

The Serbian Health Ministry said in its daily 3 pm bulletin on Thursday that 14 people died of coronavirus-related ailments over the previous 24 hours, bringing the total number of deaths to 15,647. It said that 16,675 people had been tested over the previous 24 hours, including 2,362 who tested positive for the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. The total number of people tested to date stands at 8,989,852 with 1,949,953 confirmed cases. The bulletin said that there are 970 hospitalised cases, including 47 patients on ventilators. 

Source: Rts.rs, Rtv.rs 

 

12,500 Ukrainian refugees passed through Serbia 

The RTS reported on Thursday that some 12,500 refugees from Ukraine came to Serbia since the war started in the country, adding that about 2,500 have chosen to stay in the country. Refugee Commissariat official Nikola Sakan told the RTS that Commissariat teams are deployed at three border crossing with Hungary to provide information to the refugees. We hand out brochures in Ukrainian with phone numbers and an e-mail address to contact at any time if they have problems or need information, he said, adding that they also hand out food and hygiene products. According to Sakan, most of the refugees are women with children, mainly in transit but some choose to stay in Serbia with friends and family. He said that about 30 refugees are housed in Commissariat centres. 

Source: 021.rs

"It is very important for Austria that we work together because we are equally affected by the phenomenon of organised crime and the phenomenon of illegal migration.  Serbian Politics 

 

Petkovic: 2004 pogrom was aimed at obliterating all traces of Kosovo Serbs' existence 

The head of the Serbian government Office for Kosovo and Metohija Petar Petkovic on Thursday said March 17, 2004 was one of the most difficult days in Serbia's recent history as, on that day, ethnic Albanians in Kosovo had been aiming to obliterate all traces of the existence of Serbs in the province. "In an outburst of hatred, attacks and a wave of violence by ethnic Albanian extremists, 19 people were killed, 4,012 Serbs were expelled from their ancestral homes, 935 Serb homes were destroyed and 35 churches, monasteries and monastery dwellings, including some mediaeval ones, were burned down and razed," Petkovic told the RTS, adding that the pogrom had taken place "right in front of the eyes of the international community." He said the Church of Our Lady of Ljevis - included in a UNESCO list of world cultural heritage - had been burned down as well. "Those who had the duty to protect the Serb population in Kosovo and Metohija looked on as that population fled to escape hordes of Albanian extremists. March 17 is a stain on the face of the international community," Petkovic said, adding that no one had been called to account for the plight of Serbs and the torching of Serbian Orthodox churches and monasteries. He said Serbia insisted on justice being served. "Until the murderers and those who gave the orders are found, the government will not give up on the quest for truth and justice. The ideology of hatred of 2004 was a very coordinated action aimed at expelling the Serb population," Petkovic said. The March 17-18, 2004 pogrom was, in fact, the second large pogrom committed by the ethnic Albanians against the Kosovo Serbs, the first one being the mass expulsion that followed the 1999 NATO bombing of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

Where are the Russians fleeing through the "Serbian door"? Which destinations are the most interesting for them? 

Russian carriers do not fly to Europe due to EU sanctions, which Brussels imposed due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and European carriers do not fly to Russia. By rejecting the sanctions, Serbia has become an air corridor, open to Russian citizens who are fleeing their homeland en masse through the "Serbian door". Russians who fly to Serbia often do not stay there, but travel further to Europe. According to the analysis of the travel agency Forwardkeys, in the first week of March, compared to the week before the Russian invasion of Ukraine, occupancy on flights between Russia and Serbia increased by 50 percent, and compared to the period before the pandemic, demand increased by 200 percent. "In our analysis, the speed with which Serbia became the starting point for travel between Russia and Europe stands out the most," said Olivier Ponti, the agency's vice president. Air Serbia currently flies to Russia 15 times a week, three times a week. Russians who land in Serbia often do not stay there, but travel further to Europe, according to the analysis of Forwardkeys, their final destinations are primarily Montenegro, Cyprus, France, Switzerland and Italy, less "popular" are Spain, Germany, Austria and Slovenia.

First container shipment on the Danube to the Port of Constanta 

DP World Novi Sad has successfully completed the testing of the first container shipment on the Danube between the ports of Novi Sad in Serbia and Constanta in Romania. The first ship, Vigilla, transported over 50 containers to the Port of Novi Sad last weekend, where the goods were quickly and successfully loaded onto trucks for the delivery to end customers, the company says in a press release. This is the first step toward the establishment of the new DP World Novi Sad service, which will secure a safer and simpler ecological transport of goods for the customers. DP World, a leading provider of smart logistics solutions in the world, became the owner of the Port of Novi Sad in May 2019 and obliged to invest EUR 35 million in a range of extensions and development, such as the new service of the transport on the Danube to the Port of Constanta. The company is also building a new container terminal at the port, which includes the construction of new silos for the storage of goods, the reconstruction of roads and the expansion of the vertical dock. 

Source: Rtv.rs, Tanjug.rs 

 

Crude sunflower seed oil exempted from export ban 

The Serbian government adopted today the amended Decree on limiting the prices of petroleum products, which allows companies specialising in trade in motor and other fuels at petrol stations to deliver fuel not only by filling the tanks of vehicles, but also by pouring the fuel into vessels for the transport of petroleum products in the maximum amount of 60 litres. This enables, first and foremost, farmers who use agricultural machines as means of work to continue to perform their work without hindrance. The current decision, as well as changes to this decision, have been made in order to prevent major disturbances and preserve the living standards of the population. The Serbian government also adopted the amended Decision on the temporary ban on the export of basic agricultural food products important to the population, which exempts crude oil from sunflower seed or saffron from the export ban, given that this product cannot be further used for processing into refined sunflower oil and is most commonly used in the paint and varnish industry. It was also decided to add refined sunflower oil to the list of products whose export is temporarily banned.
